title: Triple Trouble
reviewNotes: Three short branches compare the seven-piece diagrams after Qxd4+ in the bishop variation at 118s and queen variation at 76s. Bxd4 is the unique win-preserving reply and leaves Kb4 legal; Qxd4 in the queen version is actual stalemate. Independent Ka5 loses for White. Earlier nine/eight-piece promotion choices and triple-bishop mates are not certified from this terminal capture comparison.
transcript: White is only one step away from getting [music] a new queen, but black has an entire queen and white is only left with two [music] bishops. And actually, after queen to h1 with a check, black can pick up this pawn and stop the promotion. But the truth here is that fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius will be able to find the incredible [music] win that white has in this position. Because at first glance, it seems like white can still get to queen defended by the bishop, but this is a mistake. You see, black doesn't have to take the queen. Instead, he's going to collect the light square bishop. And with the two extra pawns, this is going to be a drawn end game. But luckily for white, he can throw in bishop to e6 check, saving the bishop. And if the king moves, for example, to c2, now he would be able to get a new queen. Because now the black queen has no bishop to collect. And if he trades off with the white queen, this, with some precision, is going to be enough for white to win the game. But black is not that naive. And actually, after bishop to e6 check, he goes to a3. A move that at first glance doesn't seem to change anything in the position, but this is actually setting up a trap. Because if white [music] now promotes to a queen, there is going to be the brilliant counter shot, queen takes d4, forking the king and queen and sacrificing the black queen. But actually, after we capture it, this position, out of nowhere, is going to be a stalemate and thus a draw. So, is this it? Is black simply out of the woods in this position? Well, not exactly. White has the utterly incredible [music] under promotion to a bishop and will end in this mind-blowing position where white has three bishops against one queen. And very conveniently, there is no way to check the white king. All of these lines are covered by these pieces. And if you sacrifice the queen for the bishop, this time this is not a stalemate and white is going to be able to convert. And as it turns out, that's the last concern of black. White is threatening a bunch of checkmates. For example, after something like queen to g5, there's going to be bishop to b2 check, forcing the king to go to b4 and this >> [music] >> would be a triple bishop checkmate. But the most beautiful conclusion to this position in my opinion is what happens if black tries to defend against that checkmate. Because incredibly, bishop to c5 is another beautiful checkmate. >> [music]
